newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco airport panel oks rail project funds.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco airport panel oks rail project funds.

text.p: The San Francisco Airports Commission has agreed to provide up to $200 million toward a $1.2 billion rail extension project, an airport spokesman said Thursday.
San Francisco International Airport spokesman Ron Wilson said up to $200 million would be used for on-airport improvements related to the massive Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) District project.
Wilson said the airport would use landing fees and other operating revenues to cover its portion of the project.
The commission's approval of the airport contribution should "pave the way for the acceptance by the federal government of the balance of the funding," Wilson said.
Earlier this month, the Federal Aviation Administration authorized the airport to contribute the funds to the $1.2 billion project, which will extend BART to the airport.
Under the funding plan for the project, the Federal Transit Administration would provide $750 million.
The San Francisco airport will provide $200 million, the state some $108 million and the San Mateo County Transit District about $99 million.
The remaining $10 million would come from bridge funds, project planners said.

Under federal rules, the airport is not allowed to spend airport revenues on non-airport projects. In this case, airport officials argued that the rail extension would benefit the airport and, therefore, was an appropriate expenditure.
The extension is scheduled to be completed by 2000, project planners said.
